Reported WITH its workaround rather than instead of it, which is the standing consumer rule working as intended, and the first live instance of R-4a. | ready | s | nothing — ruled by o-prime 2026-08-09; no urgency for plan 080 (koala's workaround holds and its fork is deleted in phase 3), matters for every other consumer of the standalone CLI | pij-related-koala (found and reported it, with the workaround disclosed); pij-certain-crab (reproduced on a minimal fixture, found the rm one-way door and the shared-reason-code root cause); pij-mental-dajeil (the field-versus-section probe that decided it) | THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT, and it is stronger than anything either seat reasoned to: DD ALREADY HAS IMPLICIT-CREATE SEMANTICS AT THE FIELD LEVEL AND HAS SHIPPED THEM ALL ALONG. One fixture, one schema, one verb, two levels — `dd set d.dd.json#notes` on a declared-but-absent SECTION refuses E450, while `dd set d.dd.json#rows/r-1/note hello` on a declared-but-absent FIELD returns ok and `dd get` then shows {id: r-1, note: hello}. Same "declared but not yet instantiated" state, opposite answers. SO IMPLICIT CREATE IS NOT A WIDENING OF THE WRITER CONTRACT, IT IS THE REMOVAL OF AN INCONSISTENCY — which inverts the strongest objection against it (that `set` on a declared-but-misspelled name would create rather than refuse: that is ALREADY LIVE for fields and evidently acceptable). Consistency can only resolve one way, because the other direction — refusing absent fields too — would break every consumer setting an optional field on an existing row, which is ordinary use. ROOT CAUSE: src/mutate/locate.ts refuses at :33 (`schema declares no section X` — genuinely unknown) and at :36 (`the document has no section X` — declared, creatable) with THE SAME reason code `section-unknown`, the same E450/DD_MUTATION_TARGET_INVALID, and the same next_action. The two states differ only in free-text prose, so a machine consumer must string-match the message to tell "does not exist" from "not created yet" — the exact failure the envelope exists to prevent, and one this repository refuses in three other places. At :36 the declaration is already in hand and is discarded. RULED (o-prime, 2026-08-09), three parts: (1) SPLIT THE REASON CODES — unconditional, ship it even if the rest is deferred, and the next_action must differ too (`dd schema show` is correct for genuinely-unknown and a CIRCLE for declared-but-absent, since it displays the very declaration the refusal denies). (2) IMPLICIT CREATE on set/add for a declared section — validation already runs pre-write, so a created section is schema-checked exactly like any other mutation. (3) NO `dd section add` verb — it would add public surface for something set/add already mean, and the curated-surface ruling of the same morning says every addition is an API review; this one does not earn it. |
| wl-0018 | A proxied registry makes local `npm audit` systematically more OPTIMISTIC than reality | Measured 2026-08-09 by two seats independently. The same commit and the same package-lock produce different audit verdicts depending on which registry the runner talks to: locally (packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io) 0 fixable; in CI (registry.npmjs.org) 1 fixable. DETECTION is not lagged — both registries report the same advisories — but REMEDIABILITY is: the fixed versions do not EXIST on the proxy, so npm computes fixAvailable:false and reports nothing to do. The proxy nanoid 3.3.x line ends at 3.3.16, THE VULNERABLE ONE; 3.3.17 returns 404 there, and registry.npmjs.org is unreachable from either seat (ENOTCONN). So a developer running npm audit on a proxied machine is told there is nothing actionable when in fact there is — and NOTHING IN THE OUTPUT SAYS WHICH REGISTRY PRODUCED THE VERDICT. That is this plan's parent defect (two states sharing one observable) with the environment as the hidden variable, inside a security tool. | idea | s | nothing for the write-up; the nanoid instance needs a machine with public-registry access (npm audit fix --package-lock-only), which no seat in this fleet has | pij-certain-crab (found it when the audit gate reddened CI while local disagreed; measured the ENOTCONN/404 boundary); pij-mental-dajeil (reproduced both routes from a second seat and measured that the proxy 3.3.x line stops at 3.3.16) | WHAT TO ACTUALLY DO, in increasing order of effort. (1) THE CHEAP PART IS ALREADY SHIPPED: scripts/audit-gate.mjs prints `audit-gate: registry &lt;url&gt;` as its FIRST line on every run, pass or fail, so no verdict is readable without its environment. That one line is what made this diagnosable at all, and it cost nothing. (2) STATE THE CONSEQUENCE WHERE PEOPLE READ IT: on a proxied machine a local audit is NOT a substitute for the CI audit, and a local green means 'nothing actionable FROM HERE', never 'nothing actionable'. (3) The remediation route that works is the one with public-registry access — dependabot (landed at a37a20e) generates exactly this bump, but targets the DEFAULT BRANCH, so it cannot fix a topic branch. THE GENERAL FORM, worth more than the npm instance: A TOOL THAT COMPUTES 'WHAT CAN YOU DO ABOUT THIS' IS ANSWERING A QUESTION ABOUT YOUR ENVIRONMENT, NOT ONLY ABOUT THE DEFECT — it will answer differently in CI than on a laptop and never say so. Any such tool must name the environment it consulted. THIS IS NOT A CRITICISM OF THE PROXY, which exists for supply-chain reasons and is doing its job: the defect is that its effect on audit REMEDIABILITY was invisible, not that the delay exists. |
| wl-0019 | An unrecognised relation degrades to `ref` in SILENCE — so a deliberate convention and a misspelled builtin are indistinguishable | `src/core/rel.ts:24` is `isBuiltinRel(rel) ? rel : DEFAULT_REL`, and there is NO diagnostic anywhere for an unrecognised rel — three comments document the intent, none reports it. The OPEN NAMESPACE IS BY DESIGN AND SHOULD STAY: a schema may name something dd does not yet understand without being refused, and that is what makes the `satisfies-toward` convention possible with no shipped change. THE DEFECT IS THE SILENCE, NOT THE DEGRADATION. Measured 2026-08-09 against dist/plan/semantics.js, one fixture, control and negation: rel=satisfies -&gt; 1 contradiction; rel=satisfies-toward -&gt; 0 (deliberate); rel=satisfes -&gt; 0 (typo); rel=satisfy -&gt; 0 (near miss); AND rel=Satisfies -&gt; 0 (A SINGLE CAPITAL LETTER). Every one of those silently switches OFF contradiction detection for that edge, and nothing anywhere says so. THE CAPITALISED SPELLING IS THE DANGEROUS ONE: it is not a typo a reviewer notices, it reads as correct, and its effect is to disable the one inconsistency a plan document can prove about itself. This reaches every consumer — `satisfies` and BUILTIN_RELS live in src/core/constants.ts, which SHIPS; the contradiction engine that consumes them is in src/plan/, which does NOT (no ./plan in the exports map). So the vocabulary ships to everyone while the interpreter is re-implemented per consumer, and the silent-degradation surface is the shipped half. | idea | s | nothing — and deliberately NOT ruled. o-prime declined to pick a remedy on one instance, the same discipline it applied to refusing a sixth builtin relation on the same day | pij-mental-dajeil (found it while ruling on the relation question, and framed it as a finding neither the PM nor koala had); pij-certain-crab (measured the five spellings, including the capitalised one) | TWO CANDIDATE REMEDIES, both with real costs, recorded so a second instance can choose between them rather than reopening the analysis. (1) DECLARE CUSTOM RELS IN THE SCHEMA — closes it completely and keeps the namespace open, at the price of authoring burden and a schema change; an undeclared rel then becomes a genuine finding rather than a guess. (2) WARN ON A NEAR-MISS TO A BUILTIN — cheap and needs no schema change, but it is a HEURISTIC, and a heuristic guard is a new class of thing in this repository, where every other gate is exact. It would also not catch a rel that is simply invented and wrong in a way no builtin resembles. NEITHER IS OBVIOUSLY RIGHT ON n=1, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A ROW. THE CLASS, which is the reason to keep it: an unrecognised key silently discarded is the same defect `pij-related-meadowlark` reported in `sanitizeDdLink` in another repository in the same week — two codebases, one week, one shape. AND IT IS THIS PLAN'S PARENT CAUSE IN THE RELATION VOCABULARY: one observable, two meanings, with nothing in the output to separate them. The general rule it argues for: WHEN A SYSTEM DEGRADES AN INPUT IT DOES NOT RECOGNISE, THE DEGRADATION MUST BE VISIBLE SOMEWHERE, OR THE MOST DANGEROUS INPUT IS THE ONE THAT LOOKS CORRECT. |
